title.zh: 只剩诗这一处：胡适怎样把争论变成《尝试集》
title.en: Only Poetry Was Left: How an Argument Turned into Hu Shi's Book of Experiments

dek.zh: 1916年夏天，几位中国留学生为“白话能不能写诗”争到只剩最后一处分歧。胡适认定只有以身作则，决定自己去试。
dek.en: In the summer of 1916 a few Chinese students in America had argued down to one last disagreement: could poetry be written in the everyday spoken language? Hu Shi concluded that the only way was to try it himself.

paras.zh: 1916年7月，在美国留学的胡适收到一封从绮色佳寄来的信。信里说，任鸿隽、梅光迪等几位中国朋友在凯约嘉湖上划船，片云头上黑，忽然刮起风暴，大家急忙往岸边划，几乎把船弄翻，个个淋得狼狈不堪。胡适不在船上。任鸿隽把这次险事写成一首四言古诗《泛湖即事》，附在信里，请他批评。
paras.en: In July 1916 Hu Shi, then a Chinese student in the United States, received a letter from Ithaca. Some of his Chinese friends, it said — among them Ren Hongjun and Mei Guangdi — had been out rowing on Cayuga Lake when a black cloud gathered, a storm blew up and the rain came down. Rowing hard for shore, they nearly capsized and came back soaked to the skin. Hu was not in the boat. Ren had turned the adventure into an old-style poem in four-character lines, Boating on the Lake, and enclosed it, asking Hu for his criticism.

paras.zh: 胡适回信说这首诗不好：诗里夹着《诗经》式的老字，「文字殊不调和」，还有「三千年前之死语」。这句批评惹恼了两位朋友，一场争了一年多的老问题又被翻了出来，而且越吵越窄。到这年夏天，朋友们已经承认白话可以写小说、写演说，只剩一处不肯让：诗。白话能不能用来写诗？胡适接下来没有只靠辩论，而是决定自己动手去试。
paras.en: Hu wrote back that the poem was bad. It mixed archaic words of the kind found in the ancient Book of Songs with modern language, so that, in his words (translated here), its diction did not hang together; he even spoke of dead words from three thousand years ago. The remark stung two friends and reopened an argument more than a year old, one that kept narrowing. By that summer his friends granted that the spoken language would do for novels and speeches — but not for poetry. Could poetry be written in baihua, the plain spoken language? Hu's next step was not to rely on argument alone: he decided to try it himself.

paras.zh: 主张白话也能作诗的胡适，其实自称是个保守的人，常对朋友说，语言文字是世界上最保守的东西，比宗教还保守。他最坚定的对手是梅光迪，此时在哈佛随一位保守派文学批评家深造；胡适说，正是梅光迪的强烈反对，把他“逼上梁山”。另一位是在康乃尔的朋友任鸿隽，他曾作打油诗取笑胡适，湖上那首纪事诗也出自他手。
paras.en: Hu, the man arguing that it could, called himself a conservative. He used to tell his friends that language and writing are the most conservative things in the world, more conservative than religion. His most determined opponent was Mei Guangdi, then studying at Harvard under a conservative literary critic; it was Mei's fierce opposition, Hu later said, that drove him to Liangshan — the Chinese idiom for being forced by circumstances into a rebel's course. The other was Ren Hongjun, a friend at Cornell who once teased Hu in comic verse, and who had written the poem about the lake.

paras.zh: 胡适对文字问题认真起来，起因是一张小传单。留学生每月的奖学金支票信封里，常夹着一位热心改革的书记写的传单，上面写着「不满二十五岁不娶妻。」「废除汉字，改用字母！」之类的话，大家通常看一眼就丢进纸篓。约在1915年，胡适却坐下来回了张很不客气的字条，叫对方「最好闭起鸟嘴！」。字条寄出后他又懊悔，觉得不该对一位和善的改革者这样无礼，觉得够资格的人更该认真研究这个问题。他在留学生的年会上写了篇论文，说文言是「半死的语言」：“狗”字今天还在用，“犬”字已经不用了；“骑马”是日常话，“乘马”早已不通行。
paras.en: Hu's serious interest in the written language began with a leaflet. The envelopes that carried Chinese students' monthly scholarship checks often held leaflets slipped in by a reform-minded clerk, with slogans such as marry no one under twenty-five and abolish the Chinese characters for an alphabet. Most went straight into the wastebasket. Around 1915 Hu instead wrote a rude note telling the man, in effect, to shut his beak. He soon regretted it: the man was kind, and those qualified, Hu felt, should study the problem themselves. He wrote a paper for a Chinese students' conference arguing that the classical written language was half dead. Gou, dog, is still in use, he pointed out; quan, the classical word for it, is not. The everyday phrase for riding a horse lives on; the classical one has died.

heading.zh: 从一首送别诗到《尝试集》
heading.en: From a Farewell Poem to Experiments

paras.zh: 争论要从更早的一首送别诗说起。胡适准备离开康乃尔时，梅光迪正要去哈佛。胡适写了首长长的打油诗送行，塞进十一个外国人的名字，还在诗里鼓励朋友们留意中国文学今后的发展，说致力于中国文学革命，贡献不下于征服自然。任鸿隽把那些洋名字串起来，作诗嘲笑他：「文学今革命，作诗送胡生！」胡适不肯放过，在去纽约的火车上写诗回敬：「诗国革命何自始？要须作诗如作文！」也就是说，作诗要像写文章一样。他后来说，那时自己对文学革命的想法还很模糊，但这是他第一次把它写下来。梅光迪坚决反对，认为诗的文字和文的文字自古就分道而驰。胡适后来说，朋友们愈辩愈保守，他也愈辩愈激进。
paras.en: The quarrel itself had begun with a farewell poem. As Hu was preparing to leave Cornell, Mei was about to go to Harvard. Hu saw him off with a long comic poem stuffed with eleven foreign names, urging his friends to watch where Chinese literature would go next and declaring that working for a revolution in Chinese literature was no less a contribution than conquering nature. Ren strung the foreign names into a mock poem of his own about literary revolution and sending off Hu. Hu would not let it pass. On the train to New York he wrote a reply asking where a revolution in poetry should begin, and answering that poems must be written like prose. Mei objected strongly: the language of poetry and the language of prose, he held, had gone separate ways from the start. His ideas were still vague, Hu later said, but this was the first time he had put them in writing. The more his friends argued, he said, the more conservative they became, and the more radical he became.

paras.zh: 1916年二三月间，胡适想出一个说法：一部中国文学史，就是文学工具不断更换的历史，活的工具替代死的工具。他说，这个变化在唐代就开始了：先是和尚们用白话记录语录，后来宋代的哲学家也用它，老百姓又用它唱曲、编戏、写小说；元曲这样的白话文学，是老百姓在不知不觉中完成的一场文学革命。他写长信给梅光迪讲这套道理。出乎他的意料，这位保守的朋友竟欣然接受了这个历史结论。
paras.en: In February and March 1916 Hu arrived at a general idea: the history of Chinese literature was a history of changing tools, a living tool replacing a dead one. The change, he argued, had begun in the Tang dynasty. Buddhist monks first used the spoken language to record their teachers' sayings; Song philosophers adopted it; ordinary people used it for songs, plays and novels. Vernacular literature such as Yuan drama, he said, was a literary revolution the common people had carried out without knowing it. He laid this out in a long letter to Mei. To Hu's surprise, his conservative friend gladly accepted the historical conclusion.

paras.zh: 那年夏天，胡适往返都路过绮色佳，和任鸿隽等老朋友谈了许多中国问题，尤其是文学。1916年7月6日，他在日记里记下讨论中的九条，头两条是「今日之文言乃是一种半死的文字。」「今日之白话是一种活的语言。」据胡适回忆，就在记下这九条的同时，他收到了开头那封从绮色佳寄来的信；按他的说法，湖上那件事发生在7月8日。这两处日期并不完全吻合，本文照录胡适的说法。
paras.en: That summer Hu passed through Ithaca on his way to a conference and back, and talked with Ren and other old friends about China's problems, literature above all. On July 6, 1916, he wrote nine points from those talks in his diary. The first two, in translation: today's classical language is a half-dead language; today's spoken language is a living language. According to Hu's recollection, the letter from Ithaca arrived just as he was writing down those nine points; by his account, the incident on the lake took place on July 8. The two dates do not quite fit together; this article reports Hu's account as given.

paras.zh: 他对那首纪事诗的批评，引来一场风波。任鸿隽对“死语”的说法愤愤不平；更激动的是梅光迪，他路见不平，写来一封信猛烈反击。梅光迪那时正受他那位保守派老师的影响，对胡适的一切激进主张都反对到底。他认为文字必须经过第一流诗人的锻炼和美化，才能成为诗的文字。
paras.en: His criticism of the lake poem set off a storm of its own. Ren was indignant about the dead words. Mei, angrier still, rushed to his friend's defence with a heated letter; under the influence of his conservative teacher, he opposed everything radical Hu proposed. Words become poetic language, he insisted, only after first-rate poets have refined and beautified them.

paras.zh: 胡适的回答是一首约一百句的滑稽打油诗，是他一生写过最长的一首。诗里先写“老梅”大发脾气，再举了许多例子，开玩笑地驳梅光迪“文字哪有死活”的说法，还特别顺着他的话反将一军：既然文字要靠诗人锻炼，那正该由当代的诗人把俗语俗字锻炼起来，请进诗里。两位朋友读了大发雷霆，都写信取笑他想作白话诗。可胡适从信里读出一个共同的让步：白话可以写评话、故事和小说，就是不能写诗。任鸿隽说得最干脆：「白话自有白话用处（如作小说、演说等），然不能用之于诗！」
paras.en: Hu answered with a comic poem of about a hundred lines, the longest poem he ever wrote. It opened with Old Mei losing his temper, mocked his claim that words are neither living nor dead, and turned Mei's own argument against him: if words must be refined by poets, that was exactly what Hu wanted — poets of their own day should take everyday words, refine them and bring them into poetry. Both friends were furious and wrote back mocking his attempt at vernacular verse. But in their letters Hu found a shared concession: the spoken language could be used for storytelling, tales and novels, just not for poetry. Ren put it most bluntly; in translation, he wrote that the vernacular has its own uses, such as fiction and speeches, but it cannot be used for poetry.

paras.zh: 争论缩到了最后一处。用胡适的话说，朋友们「除了“诗”这个堡垒之外，其他方面已经全部向我让步了」。他把朋友们的理由排了队：一是从来没有诗人用俗语俗字作过诗，他自己也只找到一首、甚至只是一首中的几句；二是更能服人的一条，从来没有中国作家认真着实地用白话作诗，偶尔写几行，骨子里还是看不起白话。他的结论很简单：要说服朋友，只有以身作则，自己认真去试，除此之外没有别的办法。
paras.en: The argument had shrunk to one last point. In Hu's words, his friends had conceded everything to him except the fortress of poetry. He set out their reasons in order. First, no poet had ever written verse in everyday words; Hu himself could find only one poem, perhaps only a few lines of one. Second, and more convincing, no Chinese writer had ever seriously tried; poets had dropped in a few vernacular lines on a whim, while privately looking down on the spoken language. His conclusion was simple. To persuade his friends he had to set the example and seriously try writing vernacular poetry himself. There was no other way.

paras.zh: 1916年7月26日，他写信给任鸿隽，说施耐庵、曹雪芹已经证明白话可以写好小说，「今尚需人实地试验白话是否可为韵文之利器耳」。他在给朋友们的信里说，就算失败一两次、甚至无数次，也可以不断试下去，直到证明白话究竟能不能作诗为止。他还打了个比方：「我此时练习白话诗文，颇似新辟一文学殖民地。」可惜要单枪匹马前往，找不到同伴；他也给自己留了后路：如果这块新地全是不毛之地，他也许终究还要回到“文言诗国”。七月底八月初，他决定不再写旧诗词。还没写出几首白话诗，他就先给下一本诗集取好了名字：《尝试集》。
paras.en: On July 26, 1916, he wrote to Ren — paraphrased here — that Shi Nai'an and Cao Xueqin had already shown in practice that the spoken language was the right tool for the novel; what remained was for someone to test in practice whether it could be the tool of verse. Even if they failed once, twice or countless times, he told these friends, they could keep experimenting until they knew whether the vernacular could be poetry. He compared his practice in vernacular verse and prose to opening up a new literary colony. He would have to ride out alone, with no companions. And he left himself a way back: if the new land turned out to be barren, he might end his days in the old kingdom of classical poetry after all. In late July and early August he decided to stop writing classical verse. Before he had written more than a few vernacular poems, he had already named his next collection: Experiments.

paras.zh: 1916年11月，他把一年多的讨论写成文章，提出八条很温和的建议。“文学革命”这个词，在他和朋友们的诗和信里早已常见，有时是开玩笑，有时也很严肃。可这一次，题目里不用“革命”，而用“改良”和“刍议”；按他的说法，这说明是改良而非革命，同时那只是个“刍议”，而非教条式的结论。据他事后解释，这样措辞是考虑到国内老一辈保守派一定会反对。文章抄了三份，其中一份寄给了陈独秀主编的《新青年》。
paras.en: In November 1916 he turned more than a year of argument into an article with eight very moderate proposals. Literary revolution was a phrase that had often come up in his poems and letters and in his friends' letters, sometimes as a joke and sometimes in earnest. This time he kept it out of the title, which, as he put it, spoke of reform rather than revolution and offered only a tentative proposal, not a dogmatic conclusion. By his own later account, he worded it this way because he expected the older conservatives at home to object. He made three copies; one went to New Youth, the magazine edited by Chen Duxiu.

paras.zh: 1917年1月，文章在《新青年》刊出，反响很大。陈独秀本来就是坚定的革命派，随即写了《文学革命论》响应，公开支持文学革命，并说首举义旗的是他的朋友胡适，他自己高张大旗来声援。北大另一位研究古典音韵学的教授，也对这篇留学生写的文章大为赏识。他回国前的几个月，也就是1917年一二月间，这两篇文章已经成了全国讨论的热门，读者来信不断；他也把自己尝试写的白话诗寄给《新青年》刊登。至于这些白话诗，老同学赵元任常说它们“不够白”。胡适也承认，还打了个比方：裹了多年小脚的女人，就算放了脚，也回不到天足。
paras.en: The article appeared in New Youth in January 1917 and caused a great stir. Chen, already a convinced revolutionary, answered at once with an essay on literary revolution, publicly backing the cause and saying that the banner had been raised by his friend Hu, while he himself was raising it high in his support. Another Peking University professor, a scholar of classical phonology, also greatly admired the student's article. In the months before Hu returned to China, early in 1917, the two articles were a national talking point, and readers' letters kept coming; Hu also sent the vernacular poems he had been trying out to New Youth. As for those poems, his old classmate Zhao Yuanren often said they were not vernacular enough. Hu agreed, comparing himself to a woman whose feet had been bound for years: however much she loosened the bindings, she could never have natural feet again.

paras.zh: 胡适自己说，把他推上这条路的，是一连串的小意外：一首送别诗，一场湖上的险事。他一向反对用某一个原因解释所有历史，常开玩笑说，意外往往比那些包打天下的“单因”更重要。
paras.en: Hu himself said that what pushed him down this road was a chain of small accidents: a farewell poem, a scare on a lake. He distrusted theories that explain all of history by a single cause, and liked to joke that accidents often matter more than any one cause that claims to explain everything.

paras.zh: 作者推断：这段经历最有意思的地方，是胡适把一场谁也说服不了谁的争论，变成了一个可以检验的问题。“白话不能作诗”是一句绝对的话，只要写出像样的白话诗，就能动摇它；不写，再多书信也只是各说各话。他先给诗集取名《尝试集》，等于先替自己定下了要举证的任务；他还在信里先写好了失败的退路，承认结果可能证明自己错了，这让它更像一场真正的试验，而不是换个方式继续辩论。发表时他把调子放低，陈独秀随后把旗子举高。
paras.en: The author's inference: Hu turned an argument nobody could win into a question that could be tested. The claim that the spoken language cannot be poetry is absolute; a single good vernacular poem would shake it, while without poems, any number of letters would remain a standoff. By naming his collection Experiments in advance, he in effect set himself the task of supplying the proof. In his letters he also wrote down his retreat in case of failure, accepting that the result might prove him wrong — which made it a real experiment rather than the argument continued by other means. When he published, he lowered his voice, and Chen then raised the banner.

paras.zh: 结果如何，胡适晚年也讲过：1920年，北京政府教育部通令国民小学一、二年级的教材一律改用白话。1919年五四运动以后，全国学生办起四百多种小刊物，全用白话写成。他同时说，五四学生运动对中国文艺复兴运动是一种“干扰”，把一个文化运动变成了政治运动，但对传播白话文功不可没。当初他估计这场斗争总得二十五年到三十年，结果只用了四年左右，在学校里以白话代替文言就几乎完全成功了，连他自己都没有想到。他称之为“部分的胜利”，却也说自己仍不满意：四十年来，白话文始终没有成为完全的教育工具和文学工具。
paras.en: As for the result, Hu described it late in life. After the May Fourth movement of 1919, students across China started more than four hundred small publications, all in the vernacular. At the same time he said the student movement was an interference with China's cultural renaissance, turning a cultural movement into a political one, though it did great service in spreading the vernacular. He had expected the struggle to take twenty-five to thirty years; in only about four, replacing the classical language with the vernacular in schools had almost completely succeeded, which surprised even him. In 1920 the Ministry of Education of the Beijing government ordered that textbooks for the first two years of primary school be written entirely in the spoken language. He called it a partial victory — and said he was still not satisfied: in forty years the vernacular had never become a complete tool of education and literature.

paras.zh: 这段经过来自胡适晚年的口述回忆（唐德刚译注），朋友们的话都经他转述；标明“作者推断”的段落是本文的解读，唐德刚的评语另作评论看待。详细说明见文末“出处与不确定性”。
paras.en: This account comes from Hu's oral memoir, given late in life and translated and annotated by Tang Degang; his friends' words all reach us through Hu. Paragraphs marked as the author's inference are this article's reading, and Tang's remarks are treated as commentary. More under Sources and uncertainty at the end.

scenario.zh: 作者虚构的场景：一位在公司做设计的年轻人，想让父母相信转行做独立设计也能养活自己。父母说：“这行不稳定，别人能成是别人的事。”
scenario.en: A fictional scenario from the author: a young designer at a company wants to convince their parents that going independent could pay the bills. The parents reply: the work is unstable, and other people's success is other people's business.

question.zh: 对方已经承认一件事在别处可行，唯独不信它在你这里行。你是继续举别人的成功例子，还是先做一个双方都看得见的小试验？如果试，拿什么作判断标准？
question.en: When the other side already grants that something works elsewhere but not for you, do you keep citing other people's successes, or run a small experiment you can both see? And if you experiment, what should count as the test?

assumptions.zh: 父母真正担心的是收入不稳定，不是设计这一行本身；几个月内有可能接到能展示、有收入记录的委托。
assumptions.en: The parents' real worry is unstable income, not design as a career; within a few months it is possible to win commissions that can be shown, with a record of income.

steps.zh: 把争论收缩到一个点：能不能持续接到付费委托。用业余时间小规模尝试，把委托、收入和被拒的稿子记在同一张表上。事先约好标准和期限，到时一起看记录，再决定加码还是收手。
steps.en: Narrow the argument to one point: can paid commissions keep coming in? Try it on the side, logging commissions, income and rejected work in one sheet. Agree on criteria and a deadline in advance, then review the record together and decide whether to scale up or stop.

alternative.zh: 作者提出的另一种做法：继续收集同行成功的故事去说服，代价是对方总能说“那是别人”，争论永远收不拢；或者干脆辞职全力投入，代价是把一次成败当成唯一证据，失败了也没有退路。
alternative.en: Another approach the author suggests: keep collecting stories of successful peers, at the cost that the other side can always say that is someone else, so the argument never closes; or quit and go all in, at the cost of treating a single outcome as the only evidence, with nothing to fall back on.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本文只依据一本书：胡适口述、唐德刚译注《胡适口述自传》（中国文史出版社，2020）第八章。按唐德刚说明，这一章的英文稿是从胡适《四十自述》的《逼上梁山》一章节译、经胡适手订后再回译成中文的，与原文多少有出入。因此这是当事人多年后的回忆，不是当时的独立记录。梅光迪、任鸿隽的言行都经胡适转述；胡适对“改良”措辞的解释是他事后的说法。唐德刚的注释属评论：他认为“文言是半死的文字”这句口号当年摧枯拉朽，但真实性值得重新商榷；他认为白话文百分之百成功，白话诗则还未脱离“尝试”阶段；他也记下反对者觉得胡适居功太多，1956年胡适在哈佛以此讲演时，后来为他作传的格里德嗤之以鼻。这些都是唐德刚的记述，本文未另行核验。标为“作者推断”的段落是本文的解读，思考题中的场景是虚构的。
uncertainty_note.en: This piece rests on one book: Hu Shi's oral memoir, translated and annotated by Tang Degang (Chinese Literature and History Press, 2020), chapter 8. As Tang explains, the English draft of this chapter was abridged from the Driven to Liangshan chapter of Hu's Forty Self-Narratives, revised in Hu's own hand and then translated back into Chinese, and it differs from the original to some degree. It is therefore a participant's recollection many years later, not an independent record from the time. Mei Guangdi's and Ren Hongjun's words and actions reach us through Hu, and his explanation of the moderate wording is his own later account. Tang's notes are commentary: he thought the slogan that the classical language is half dead was devastating in its day but that its truth deserves a fresh look; he judged vernacular prose a complete success and vernacular poetry not yet out of the experimental stage; and he records that Hu's opponents felt he claimed too much credit, and that when Hu gave this account in a 1956 lecture at Harvard, Jerome B. Grieder, later his biographer, scoffed. These are Tang's accounts and were not checked separately here. Paragraphs marked as the author's inference are this article's reading; the scenario in the question is fictional.

preheader.zh: 朋友们让步到只剩“诗”这一处，他没有再争，而是决定自己去试
preheader.en: When his friends conceded everything but poetry, he stopped arguing and decided to run the experiment himself
